faq.q: What meme layouts and templates can I start from?
faq.a: Six layouts are built in: Top/Bottom classic, 2-Panel Compare, 4-Panel Grid, Drake (2 rows), Speech Bubble and Demotivational. There are also six programmatic template backgrounds like Drake Format, Distracted BF, Change My Mind, Expanding Brain, Two Buttons and This Is Fine. You can also upload your own image, drop several at once to fill panels, or build a solid, gradient or blank canvas.

faq.q: How much control do I have over each text layer?
faq.a: Every text layer is independent. You can set font (Impact/Anton, Arial, Georgia, Courier, Comic Sans or Verdana), alignment, UPPERCASE toggle, size (12–140), stroke width (0–20), rotation (−180 to 180), opacity (10–100%), and separate fill and outline colours. Layers can be added, reordered, selected and deleted, and you drag them directly on the canvas to reposition.

faq.q: What export sizes and formats are available?
faq.a: You can export at the native canvas size or pick presets: Instagram Square 1080×1080, Story/Reel 1080×1920, Twitter/X 1200×675, or WhatsApp 800×800. Save as PNG (lossless) or JPEG, with a quality slider from 30 to 100 that only applies to JPEG. The tool shows an estimated file size before you download.

faq.q: Does it keep my past memes and edits?
faq.a: Yes. Your working state autosaves to browser localStorage, so reopening the tool restores your last meme. Each download is also added to a Recent Memes gallery that keeps up to 8 thumbnails; click one to reload that meme's full state. There's also Undo/Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) with up to 30 steps. Everything stays in your browser with no upload.
